text: {"findings":[{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N11","page":1,"quote":"HEAT TREATMENT  :-(English) 1) TO BE HARDENED UPTO 32-35 HRC. 2) RETAPPING TO BE DONE AFTER SURFACE TREATMENT AT SUPPLIER END.( IF APPLICABLE )"}],"comment":"The note specifies hardness and that retapping must occur after surface treatment, but it does not state whether hardening is to be performed before or after machining the part's functional features. The designer should add a clear sequence (e.g., 'machine, then harden, then finish-grind') so the shop knows when to apply the heat treatment relative to final dimensions.","recommended_correction":"Update N11 to specify the manufacturing stage at which the 32-35 HRC hardening applies (e.g., after rough machining, before final grinding)."},{"rule_id":"WPS-004","evidence":[{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D4","page":1,"quote":"⌀12 H7"},{"kind":"note","ref":"N2","page":1,"quote":"# FINISH: I.Z.B.P. (TRIVALENT)"}],"comment":"The ⌀12 H7 hole (D4) carries a tight fit tolerance, yet the drawing calls for trivalent zinc plating (N2) without any allowance for the plating thickness on this bore. Plating buildup will shrink the hole below its H7 limit, causing the mating pin or sensor to no longer fit. The designer should either mask the H7 bore during plating or adjust the pre-plate dimension to account for the coating thickness.","recommended_correction":"Add a note specifying that the ⌀12 H7 hole is to be masked during plating, or revise D4 to a pre-plate size that accommodates the specified I.Z.B.P. coating thickness while still achieving H7 after plating."}]}
